chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: There is no manumission for the believer after death.
And manumission is not valid except during life.
ai.seo_question: Does manumission of a slave take effect after death in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this ruling to distinguish manumission (itq) from bequest (wasiyya), clarifying that it is an immediate act of ownership transfer requiring the master's life, unlike a will which takes effect posthumously. This distinction is crucial in Shia jurisprudence for determining the status of the slave and the distribution of the master's estate upon death.
